question: What is the medical term for earwax removed during irrigation?
explanation: Cerumen is the natural waxy substance produced in the external auditory canal that can sometimes become impacted. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why is ear irrigation performed before a routine physical examination?

options.A: To treat an active middle ear bacterial infection
options.B: To measure the exact internal temperature of the brain
options.C: To prevent permanent nerve deafness in older adults
options.D: To clear blocked wax so the eardrum is visible

explanation: Clearing impacted wax allows the healthcare provider to clearly see the tympanic membrane during an otoscopic examination. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h1)

question: A patient with which condition must NEVER undergo standard ear irrigation?
explanation: Introducing fluid through a hole in the eardrum carries infection and trauma directly into the middle ear. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h2)

question: What happens when water touches an organic foreign body like a seed in the ear canal?

options.A: The object dissolves instantly into harmless liquid
options.B: The seed starts to germinate inside the ear canal
options.C: The object swells and becomes harder to remove
options.D: The object floats to the top for easy scooping

explanation: Organic matter absorbs moisture, expands significantly, and tightly wedges itself deeper into the narrow canal. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h2)

question: What temperature should the irrigation fluid be before starting?
explanation: Using fluid that is too cold or too hot triggers the vestibular system, causing severe dizziness and nausea. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why is the patient asked to hold the kidney basin during irrigation?

options.A: To measure the exact volume of fluid put into the ear
options.B: To maintain proper balance while sitting on the examination chair
options.C: To keep their hands busy so they do not touch the syringe
options.D: To catch returning water and dislodged wax effectively

explanation: Holding the basin snugly against the neck and jaw catches all runoff and keeps the patient dry. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h3)

question: How do you position the adult pinna to straighten the ear canal?
explanation: Pulling the adult pinna up and back straightens the external auditory canal for better fluid entry. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h4)

question: Where should the stream of water be directed inside the ear canal?

options.A: Against the floor of the canal only
options.B: Directly at the center of the eardrum
options.C: Against the side wall of the canal
options.D: Deep into the middle ear cavity

explanation: Directing water along the canal wall safely sweeps wax out without putting excessive pressure on the eardrum. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h4)

question: What is the primary cause of sudden dizziness during ear irrigation?

options.A: Pulling the pinna upward during the procedure
options.B: Using normal saline instead of plain tap water
options.C: Holding the kidney basin too firmly on the neck
options.D: Fluid temperature differing from body temperature

explanation: Temperature imbalances affect the inner ear balance organs, causing sudden caloric vertigo and nausea. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h5)

question: What should the nurse do first if a patient experiences severe pain during irrigation?
explanation: Pain indicates potential trauma or pressure injury, requiring immediate cessation of fluid delivery. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h5)

question: What detail must be included in the nursing documentation after ear irrigation?

options.B: Appearance and amount of removed debris
options.C: Exact brand name of the plastic basin
options.D: Name of the nurse who trained the student

explanation: Recording what came out helps evaluate the effectiveness of the wax removal procedure. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h6)

question: Why is a final otoscopic check performed at the end of the procedure?

options.A: To measure the exact diameter of the outer ear opening
options.B: To confirm the canal is clear and the eardrum is safe
options.C: To check if any irrigation fluid remains in the middle ear
options.D: To verify that the patient's hearing has improved instantly

explanation: Inspecting the canal afterwards ensures the impactions are gone and no accidental trauma occurred. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T11#GNS122_U1_T11_h6)
